title: Product degree equals spectral degree
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis on $\Omega$ indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$. For every function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, its product degree equals its spectral degree with respect to $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$B$ is a finite Fourier basis indexed by a finite nonempty set
